title: Precise synthesis of targeted noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.

recollection.starting_material: Likely a mixed solution of noble-metal salts such as HAuCl4, H2PtCl6, PdCl2, RhCl3, and IrCl3 (or similar precursors) dissolved in an organic or aqueous medium together with surfactants or capping ligands.
recollection.intervention: Probable one-pot co-reduction or solvothermal synthesis in which all metal ions are simultaneously reduced by a strong reductant (e.g., NaBH4, hydrazine, or polyol), with careful control of temperature, concentration, and ligand environment to achieve equimolar incorporation—possibly aided by stepwise precursor injection or seed-mediated growth to ‘target’ specific compositions.
recollection.structure: Ultrafine (≈2–5 nm) single-phase face-centered cubic high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles composed entirely of noble metals, showing random atomic distribution without phase segregation.
recollection.mechanism: High configurational entropy stabilizes the random solid-solution phase; rapid, concurrent reduction combined with ligand protection prevents sequential nucleation and segregation, yielding homogeneous alloying at the nanoscale.
recollection.results: Energy-dispersive X-ray and STEM mapping likely confirmed uniform elemental distribution; XRD showed a single fcc peak shift relative to the pure metals. Reported catalytic mass activities perhaps 3–5× higher than commercial Pt/C for the oxygen reduction reaction and enhanced stability over 10 000 potential cycles. Average particle size ~3 nm, narrow size distribution (<10% RSD), and composition within ±2 at.% of the targeted equimolar ratio.

score.note: The recollection describes a speculative ligand-assisted co-reduction/solvothermal route rather than the actual spray-drying and H2 thermal decomposition-reduction process. It incorrectly identifies 2–5 nm all-noble-metal fcc nanoparticles instead of porous 3D nanoframeworks containing noble and transition metals with composition-dependent fcc/hcp phases. The proposed entropy/concurrent-reduction mechanism conflicts with the sequential noble-metal-seeded hydrogen reduction mechanism and Pt–Ru phase transformation. All quantitative claims concern invented particle sizes, ORR activity, and cycling rather than the reported MOR activity (2637 mA/mgPt), ECSA (104.4 m2/gPt), and phase-transition temperatures.
